extracted.intended_audience: researchers and stakeholders (potential grantees, national-lab users, policymakers, general public)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the mission, priorities, capabilities, and impact expectations of the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science, intended to communicate what kinds of research, facilities, partnerships, and outcomes the Office values and supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to expanding human knowledge and driving discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: "Science is about service – about a commitment to expanding human knowledge and driving discovery."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office frames science as service to the nation; research supported should advance fundamental understanding and enable discovery rather than only short-term product development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for basic research in the physical sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: "We are the nation’s largest supporter of basic research in the physical sciences."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to fundamental research in physical sciences across scales and disciplines (e.g., particle physics, condensed matter, materials, astrophysics) rather than primarily to applied or mission-specific development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stewardship of national laboratories
rubrics_metrics.description: "The steward of 10 of the Nation’s national laboratories"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office is responsible for managing and enabling the national lab system; proposals and activities that leverage or strengthen lab capabilities and infrastructure align with this stewardship role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for the Nation’s best minds using world-class facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Office of Science supports the Nation’s best minds, using the world’s best facilities, to keep America at the forefront of discovery."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office emphasizes funding and access for top researchers and teams to use premier facilities; competitiveness, excellence of personnel, and use of high-end infrastructure are implicit selection considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration of discovery via major scientific user facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Office of Science accelerates discovery with the world’s largest array of major scientific user facilities that includes particle colliders, powerful X-ray light sources, and delicate sensors and optics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision, operation, and user-access of large scientific facilities (e.g., colliders, light sources, supercomputers) is central; projects that require or expand such user-facility capabilities are within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on cutting-edge computing and exascale/quantum initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: "Some of the most powerful supercomputers in the world reside in DOE user facilities... Today, we’re focused on the future of computing, pushing computing speeds to exascale and re-imagining... computing based on quantum physics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority areas include high-performance computing, exascale readiness, and quantum information science; proposals that advance computational capability, large-scale simulation, or quantum technologies align with these emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad, discovery-driven research across scales (from astronomy to nanoscale)
rubrics_metrics.description: "From astronomy to zeolites, our researchers are unveiling secrets of the basic building blocks of matter... They peer deep into outer space... They peer deep into inner space, too, examining and manipulating matter at nanoscale and atomic resolutions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office endorses a wide scope of fundamental inquiry spanning the very large to the very small; interdisciplinary and multi-scale basic science are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fostering innovation, technology development, and economic progress
rubrics_metrics.description: "This commitment... is what makes the Department of Energy’s (DOE’s) Office of Science an indispensable pillar of America’s leadership in science and technology... Discovery science provides an enduring foundation for technological innovation and economic progress."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should have potential to enable downstream innovation and economic benefits; examples (drug discovery, materials, batteries) illustrate desirable translational pathways and technology transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and engagement with industry and small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: "More than 40 Fortune 500 companies and dozens of small businesses use our facilities each year, leveraging these unique tools and capabilities..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages collaborations and facility use by industry and small businesses; projects that enable or demonstrate industry engagement, technology commercialization, or user-industry partnerships are aligned with Office goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of real-world societal impacts and solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Page lists concrete societal impacts (e.g., contributions to drug development, Alzheimer’s insights, veteran health, airport security, cancer therapy, safe water) as outcomes of Office-supported research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While basic research is central, the Office highlights and values research that leads to tangible societal benefits—public health, security, environmental remediation, and industrial applications are visible examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive national laboratory system as a strategic resource
rubrics_metrics.description: "The DOE laboratory system is the most comprehensive research system of its kind in the world, and constitutes a critical strategic scientific and technical resource."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The labs are positioned as unique national assets; proposals that leverage, sustain, or enhance the lab system’s comprehensive capabilities and strategic value are consistent with Office priorities.
